name: 3 Steps to Spanish Fluency: Online Workshops Austin
description:
This group is for people wishing to learn Spanish to a high level of competency, especially if they have had trouble progressing in the past and are looking for a new way to improve.
The group workshops are hosted by Francis Collier and are free and open to anyone interested.
More information on paid courses is available at the end of the workshop for anyone looking to improve further.
The 3 Step Process:
Step 1: The 12 Sounds.
In Spanish there are 12 new sounds that do not exist in English.
The first step in the process to fluency is to learn ALL of these sounds CORRECTLY.
If you don't know what all of these sounds are please be advised Francis Collier will take everyone through them in the workshop.
Step 2: Native Phrases.
Very often Spanish learners when presented with a native level conversation find it sounds "too fast" and they can't keep up.
Commonly there are two things that are going wrong in this step.
Reason 1. The 12 new sounds in Spanish have not been learnt and therefore the fundamental building blocks required are not there.
Reason 2. The student cannot recognise the Native Phrases used as they do not know them and have not practised recognising them. This can often happen because the student is still translating in their head from English.
What are Native Phrases?
They are combinations of words that are used so commonly in a language that they are squeezed together and said very quickly.
Think of the way someone might say “What do you want?” to their friend if they are in a drive through. It’s more like “wadayawan?”
It’s exactly the same in Spanish, there are many native phrases that native speakers say every day and practising to recognise these at speed is crucial in order to understand real conversation.
Step 3: Real Conversations at Native Speed.
The third step is to practise in a conversation at REAL Native Speed.
Imagine learning to play baseball and spending hours reading books on base ball, watching and analysing old games but never playing a real game at real speed.
How long do you think it would take to get good?
This being a bad idea seems very obvious in the example above but this is what so many students do with apps and books and movies when learning a language and many of them never reach fluency with this approach.
So if you are interested in coming along and learning more about the process to Spanish fluency and how to improve your Spanish then please sign up for one of our workshops.
To sign up for the workshop go to the event page and click the on "Attend" button for the workshop link.
Good luck and we hope to see you soon.
As perpolicy: Attendees under the age of 18 must have a guardian with them.

name: Introduction to The Gurdjieff Work
description:
The aim of this Meet Up is to help people approach and appreciate the psychological ideas ofthe Gurdjieff Work. This is a public discussion forum rather than a "lecture style" meeting. However, itmixesboth elements. The intended form of the meeting is:
• Each meeting lasts about 90 minutes.
• Meetings are led by a member of the group, usually the group leader.
• Each meeting is themed around the discussion of a particularconcept from The Work.
• Questions and exchanges of ideas are invited and welcomed.
• The intention is that attendees acquire a deeper knowledge of The Work from the meeting.
It is advised that only people who have some familiarity with The Gurdjieff Work (for example those who have at the very least read about it) attend. The meeting assumes at least a little knowledge. However, It is not absolutely necessary to have read any of the books written directly by Gurdjieff, but experience of this may help.
The Meet Up is usually led by Robin Bloor. His lineage is that he was (from 1988) a pupil of Rina Hands, who was herself a pupil both of P.D. Ouspensky and G. I. Gurdjieff.
He is also the author of the two books;To Fathom The Gist Volume 1: Approaches to The Writings of G. I. Gurdjieff, and To Fathom The Gist Volume 2: The Arch-Absurd.
Gurdjieff's magnum opus, Beelzebub's Tales to His Grandson is, perhaps, the only example of Objective Literature available to us in our time. Reading it requires both effort and knowledge, but it is accessible.

name: Russian/Eastern European poetry exchange
description:
We started our poetry exchange meetings early in 2015 to present our own poems and share samples of contemporary Russian poetry. Since then, we have been meeting approximately once in a month, each time with a selected major topic or author to present. We accept all Slavic languages, contemporary, ancient and formation-stage (e.g. Siberian).
We usually read in rounds; responses to the previous reader are welcome but not obligatory. Bring your own masterpieces, or your friends', or any verses you'd like to share, or bring nothing and just come to attend - there is no obligatory degree of participation:) Both native speakers and language learners are welcome; translation service is provided on demand.
We don't promise exhaustive coverage of Russian or Eastern European poetry, but do promise abroadcoverage of it. If you think we are undeservedly underserving a particular topic, let us know, or simply come and share - we love collaborative research!
Let you know if you'd like to see a poem translated to/from Russian or Ukrainian.

name: Austin Storytelling Events
description:
This is a meetup for all those who love telling stories or hearing them told. While other arts have evolved or changed throughout history, oral storytelling, the world's original art form, remains largely the same. With the human voice as its brush, and the evening campfire, mountain path, or busy city square as its canvas, no two stories are alike: audience, orator, and environment combine to create a unique and unforgettable moment in history. It is the art of caves and castles, of weddings and war-time, whether sitting in front of grandpa's chair or speaking at his funeral: storytelling unites us.
A little about me: I am a full-time Chinese-English translator with a background in education and a Master's in Taiwanese Folklore Studies from UT. I teach a Chinese class at Southwestern University and enjoy solo hikes, running groups, and watching the never-ending cycle of Star Wars shows on Disney+ with my girlfriend. While my background is in myth/folklore, I am passionate about community storytelling events like The Moth and Hyde Park Storytelling, and I always do my best to attend them when I can.
The goal is to host small, simple outdoor storytelling events once or twice a week at various locations around Austin, where people can gather, enjoy a beverage, and listen to each other's stories. We will have "Story Practice" events, chances to improve your skills and gain confidence, and I will post my more formal events where I will be speaking at UT, Southwestern, etc.
For practice events, storytellers can simply show up, tell a story or just join in on our discussion, and get feedback from people if they so choose. I will begin with an introduction to the theme for the night, then we will move into informal brainstorming activities designed to familiarize ourselves with each other and get the creative juices flowing. You can prepare a short 5-10 minute history, personal narrative, folk or fairy tale, etc., but you're more than welcome to just come and listen. All are welcome, no exceptions. Events and times will be posted on Meetup.
We hope to see you there!

name: Austin Mahjong Social Club
description:
Welcome Mahjong lovers! This group is for Austin, Texas and surrounding cities. If you do not reside in this area and do not plan on attending the events, please do not join this group.
We are a couple of Hong Kong style Mahjong players looking for beginner and advanced players to join our group. We welcome players who want to share and coach their Mahjong versions like American, Japanese, Vietnamese, etc, style Mahjong. We mostly play Hong Kong / Chinese style right now, and it's very easy to learn. Please don't be afraid to join. We will expand to more versions as we get volunteer coaches. Let us know if you want to lead a mahjong game. We can certainly use the help.
Group rulesYou must RSVP in order to play.
We need four players for Mahjong. When RSVPs are three or less, we may cancel the game. Each event has space for 4 to 8 players, and if all 8 are attending, we can have two tables. Mahjong is played with a table of four. If you don't show up, it affects everyone's ability play. For this reason we now track "no shows" and two no shows will be permanently removed from the group. Also, if you join a game, and then cancel after the close of the RSVPs, it's difficult for people on the waitlist to join. They have usually made other plans. If you cancel late, it will be counted as a "no show." So please plan accordingly. Please be courteous to the organizers and other members.
If you change your mind about attending, please change your RSVP to "not going." Please check your Meetup messages the night before the event for updates or changes to the event. We often move the first four players on the WAITLIST. If you are one of the first four people on the waitlist, and you can't make it, please remove yourself from the waitlist.
The best way to learn Mahjong is by playing. But if you're shy or nervous about starting, you can come and observe the game. Please post in the event comments if you want to do that so we can get to know you. You don't have to RSVP.
Mahjong!

name: Austin LangChain - AI & LLM
description:

Are you a AI / LLM enthusiast who finds the power of LangChain fascinating? Are you currently learning and utilizing this innovative technology? Look no further! Our meetup group is the perfect platform for you to connect with like-minded individuals in the Austin area who share your passion for LangChain.
Whether you're a beginner eager to dive into the world of LangChain or an experienced user looking to expand your knowledge, our group provides an inclusive and supportive environment for all levels of expertise. Join us to engage in enlightening discussions, share valuable insights, and collaborate on exciting projects related to LangChain.
Here's what you can expect from our meetup group:
Informative Presentations:We regularly host presentations by industry experts, researchers, and practitioners who will share their expertise and insights into the latest advancements in LangChain. These talks will cover various aspects, including best practices, practical applications, and future trends.
Hands-on Workshops:Get ready to roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty! We organize interactive workshops that allow you to put your knowledge into practice. Learn how to leverage LangChain effectively through practical exercises, coding sessions, and collaborative problem-solving activities.
Networking Opportunities:Connect with fellow language enthusiasts, developers, researchers, and professionals who are passionate about LangChain. Expand your professional network, exchange ideas, and foster meaningful connections that can potentially lead to exciting collaborations or career opportunities.
Project Showcases:Share your LangChain projects and see what others have been working on. Our group provides a platform for members to showcase their creations, seek feedback, and receive support and encouragement from the community. This is a fantastic opportunity to gain inspiration, learn from others, and contribute to the growth of the LangChain ecosystem.
Q&A Sessions and Discussions:Have burning questions or specific topics you'd like to explore? Our meetups include interactive Q&A sessions and group discussions where you can seek clarifications, share your experiences, and engage in thought-provoking conversations about LangChain and its applications.
Join us today and become part of the vibrant Austin LangChain community! Let's learn, collaborate, and shape the future of language technology together. Whether you're a student, professional, researcher, or simply a curious individual, we welcome everyone with open arms. Together, we'll unlock the true potential of LangChain and revolutionize the way we interact with languages.
Note:This meetup group is conducted in English, and proficiency in LangChain is not a prerequisite for participation. We believe in creating an inclusive environment where everyone can learn and grow together.

Mission:G-ABC aims to create a thriving environment where international friendships and professional networks flourish. We focus on bridging the gap between Germany and the United States, providing a platform for meaningful interactions and collaboration.

Professional Networking: Connect with industry leaders, entrepreneurs, and professionals from both Germany and the United States, expanding your business horizons
Business Referral Networking: Enhance your business opportunities through a network that actively supports lead generation and partnership building
Cultural Exchange: Engage in cultural experiences through German conversation
Community & Support: Benefit from a supportive community that offers guidance on  settling into Austin life, especially if you are new in town or here for a work trip
Social Events & Happy Hours: Enjoy a variety of social events, from happy hours to online meetings, providing the perfect setting for making lasting connections and friendships

We believe in creating an approachable and relaxed environment for networking and connection-building. Our meetings are often held in conversational settings like breweries, ensuring a comfortable atmosphere for everyone. Additionally, we offer Zoom online meetings to accommodate those who prefer virtual interactions, making it easy for members to stay connected regardless of location.

We aim to bring together engineers, researchers, students, and professors from academia and industry—whether or not they currently use formal methods in their work.
Our goal is to deepen understanding, explore new ideas, collaborate on new projects, and discuss notable existing projects (like seL4, CompCert, Idris, Quickcheck, Dafny, and more). name: Austin Physics for Fun Meetup Group

description:

It's not a free graduate school or a place for amateur theoreticians to promote their ideas. So all you need is curiosity about the world we live in.
Physics has both technological and philosophical applications. We'll consider both. We'll do some of our own experiments in "fluid flow" at local bars monthly. Also we'll have physics slide shows in the library meeting rooms, followed by discussions at nearby restaurants.

name: Austin Clojure Meetup
description:
AppreciationThank you to Capital Factory for sponsoring Austin Clojure Meetup. Capital Factory is the center of gravity for entrepreneurs in Texas. They meet the best entrepreneurs in Texas and introduce them to their first investors, employees, mentors, and customers. To sign up for a Capital Factory coworking membership, click.
About Austin ClojureOur group was formed in October 2011. Since then, it has focused on Clojure and related Lisp languages, such as Common Lisp and Scheme, all of which have strongly influenced the design of Clojure and the approach Clojure takes in approaching software design.
Clojure also has Java as its foundational platform. Clojure's focus is not on the Java language but on the JVM and associated libraries. The JVM provides massive amounts of power for Clojure b/c you can use any Java library from Clojure, and it is pretty easy and clean to do so. Existing Java libraries can be wrapped in a functional approach with Clojure, thus providing a more functional and data-oriented approach to using the libraries. It gives the libraries a Clojury and Lispy feel.
Group DynamicsWe encourage members who enjoy Clojure to share that passion with others by giving talks or demos of things they have been working on or have questions about. It could be a lightning talk of 5 minutes, a longer talk that takes almost an entire meeting, or something you found online and played with for a bit and think is interesting. Examples of talks include: how to write Minecraft bots, Clojure for Social Data Mining, wrapping a Java library in Clojure to make it more idiomatic to use, etc.
Another valuable and fun approach is to tag-team a talk with another group member. Often working on something together with another person makes it more fun and educational for both people as you bounce ideas and approaches off one another.
It's essential for a healthy group for all members to be engaged and contribute, so please consider sharing a talk. It'll help our group and lead to more Clojure usage. We strive to be a member-driven group, and for that to be the case, we need our members to share things they are doing and have learned.
Help us make this year the best year yet.
Thank you,
Norman Richards and Sam Griffith

description:

A table for 4 to 8 is the perfect recipe (😏) for the best of conversations. This creates enough variety of personalities, thoughts, feelings and experiences to make interesting conversations but isn’t so large as to make people feel uncomfortable or intimidated to go deep.

We explore a variety of foods and drinks in the city - everything from food trucks and hole in the walls to breweries and cocktail bars to fine dining.

We hope you will join us in our Table for 4.

Check us out on Discord: https://discord.gg/hcGFDdyWfe

name: Austin Vietnamese Circle
description:
Welcome to our Vietnamese language exchange in Austin!
Are you interested in working on your Vietnamese or English skills? Are you a Vietnamese speaker looking to help others learn Vietnamese? Are you an English speaker looking to help others learn English? Join our Meetup group!
Learn to speak Vietnamese or English in a fun environment. We will have casual conversation, a great time, and lots of laughs :) Bring a notebook or dictionary if you like!
All levels are welcome! Our group is new, so we’re open to feedback and suggestions on how to make this fun and beneficial for everyone.
Help support our restaurants by purchasing a beverage or a snack while we chat! Looking forward to meeting you!
Some(Updated over the time)
Chào mừng các bạn đến với chương trình trao đổi Việt ngữ tại Austin!
Bạn có dự tính trau giồi kỹ năng sử dụng Việt ngữ hay Anh ngữ không?  Bạn có phải là người Việt muốn giúp người khác học tiếng Việt không? Bạn có phải là người Mỹ muốn giúp người khác học tiếng Anh không? Mời bạn tham gia chương trình Hội Họp và Học Hỏi với chúng tôi!
Luyện nói tiếng Việt hoặc tiếng Anh trong khung cảnh vui để học. Chúng tôi sẽ có đàm thoại giản dị trong không khí vui tươi, thoải mái, thú vị. Bạn có thể mang theo sổ tay ghi chép hoặc từ điển nếu muốn.
Mọi trình độ đều được hoan nghênh! Vì là nhóm mới thành lập, chúng tôi sẵn sàng đón nhận ý kiến và đề nghị nhằm phát triển chương trình cho hay hơn và hữu ích cho tất cả.
Chúng ta vừa trò chuyện vừa trợ giúp nhà hàng bằng cách mua nước uống hoặc thức ăn nhẹ.
Chúng tôi mong có cơ hội gặp gỡ các bạn!

name: Austin Women Travel: Explore the World, Build Connections
description:
We’re a vibrant community of women who share a passion for exploring the world, making authentic connections, and creating unforgettable memories. Our small-group trips aren’t just about travel—they’re about building a fun, supportive community where every adventure feels like a getaway with friends who inspire and empower you.
Join us to discover new cultures, step out of your comfort zone, and connect with women who believe that travel can transform your world. Let’s make memories, share laughs, and explore the extraordinary—together.

name: Austin Mahjong Social Club
description:
Welcome Mahjong lovers! This group is for Austin, Texas and surrounding cities. If you do not reside in this area and do not plan on attending the events, please do not join this group.
We are a couple of Hong Kong style Mahjong players looking for beginner and advanced players to join our group. We welcome players who want to share and coach their Mahjong versions like American, Japanese, Vietnamese, etc, style Mahjong. We mostly play Hong Kong / Chinese style right now, and it's very easy to learn. Please don't be afraid to join. We will expand to more versions as we get volunteer coaches. Let us know if you want to lead a mahjong game. We can certainly use the help.
Group rulesYou must RSVP in order to play.
We need four players for Mahjong. When RSVPs are three or less, we may cancel the game. Each event has space for 4 to 8 players, and if all 8 are attending, we can have two tables. Mahjong is played with a table of four. If you don't show up, it affects everyone's ability play. For this reason we now track "no shows" and two no shows will be permanently removed from the group. Also, if you join a game, and then cancel after the close of the RSVPs, it's difficult for people on the waitlist to join. They have usually made other plans. If you cancel late, it will be counted as a "no show." So please plan accordingly. Please be courteous to the organizers and other members.
If you change your mind about attending, please change your RSVP to "not going." Please check your Meetup messages the night before the event for updates or changes to the event. We often move the first four players on the WAITLIST. If you are one of the first four people on the waitlist, and you can't make it, please remove yourself from the waitlist.
The best way to learn Mahjong is by playing. But if you're shy or nervous about starting, you can come and observe the game. Please post in the event comments if you want to do that so we can get to know you. You don't have to RSVP.
Mahjong!

name: Austin LGBTQ foodie potluck
description: A potluck group where it creates healthy social and relaxing environment. Meet, Eat, and talk.

name: Austin Sysadmins and IT Nerds Who Like BBQ
description: I like to get together with fellow IT nerds, usually Windows network admins and IT Director types who like to eat various types of food and socialize.  I'm thinking cheeseburgers, barbecue, steak, etc.  While dining we can enjoy pleasant conversation about the idiot users we serve, technology trends, things to fix before they break, cybersecurity, new Microsoft stuff, cars, politics, why it's best to have an office where you can close the door and let the helpdesk folks handle things, etc.

name: VegAustin Potlucks
description:
You don't have to be vegan or vegetarian to attend our events, but we ask that you bring a vegan dish to our potlucks.
VegAustin Potlucks is a part of the Austin Vegan and Vegetarian Association. Visit our website atfor more information about who we are and what we do!

name: Kimbap and Krochet in the park
description:
Hi everyone! My name is Simon. I decided to create this group in hopes of bringing like minded people together to have a great time making/eating amazing Korean food (more than just kimbap), enjoying hobbies, and more random activities together!
There are two main reasons I wanted to make this group.
#1 I grew up in South Korea, and learned how to cook the cuisine like a pro, so I wanted to share my passion for it with anyone that’s interested!
#2 I feel like I need (and that most of ya’ll probably need), a dedicated time and place to actually do the things we enjoy doing.
Take a chance and come hang out with me! Worst case scenario it’s not fun at all, and you leave! 😎

name: The Austin Asian Professionals Meetup Group
description:
Meet with other local Asian Professionals to network, make new friends, and have fun! Join us if you're interested in meeting new people, making connections, and enjoying the city. All are welcome, including friends, partners, and non-Asian people!
Please be mindful with your RSVPs, especially if we have events at restaurants. We would hate to hold up business by reserving and holding more tables than we need, and your spot can be given to someone who really wants to go. We have a strict no-show policy (except on large events like festivals, night markets, etc..). You will be reminded of these rules after 1 no-show, given a warning after the 2nd no-show, and you will be removed from the group after your third no-show.
If you have an idea for an event, message Eddie Jung (the organizer) and he'll add it for everyone to enjoy!

name: Pride Plates: The ATX LGBTQIA+ Dining Club
description:
Welcome to Pride Plates: The ATX LGBTQIA+ Dining Club!
We're a mother-daughter duo, Katherine and Brooke, excited to bring together LGBTQIA+ individuals—especially young adults—and their supportive allies for fun and friendly restaurant outings in the heart of Austin.
Our goal is to create a welcoming space for everyone in the LGBTQIA+ community, along with allies who are committed to uplifting and directly supporting them. Whether you're looking to make new friends, enjoy great food, or simply connect with like-minded people, this group is for you!
We’ll focus on exploring restaurants around the UT, central Austin, and south Austin areas, discovering new flavors while building a sense of community.
Join us as we celebrate diversity, connection, and delicious dining experiences!

name: Vegan Table for 8
description:
The purpose of this group is to get small groups together to have lunch or dinner at the many incredible vegan spots around Austin.
Meetups will be limited to anywhere from 4 to 8 spots so we can more easily get to know each other and introverts will feel more comfortable sharing in a group.
Anyone who is vegan, vegetarian, vegan curious is encouraged to join.

name: Spanish and Hindi Language Exchange in Austin
location: Whole Foods at The Domain, Austin, TX
description:
This will be a Spanish/Hindi language exchange group. If you want to have conversation in Spanish or Hindi for language development then this is the group for you!!!
For the first hour we will have open conversations in Hindi. The second hour and beyond we will have conversations in Spanish.
Occasionally we will have hikes, visit museums, and experience restaurants around Austin just for added fun!

name: Subtle Asian Real Estate and Business
location: The Brewtorium Brewery & Kitchen, Austin, TX
description:
Welcome to Subtle Asian Real Estate and Business Meetup! This group is designed for Asian professionals looking to network and strategize in the fields of real estate and business.
We focus on building your real estate team, business development, and strategic planning, with a special emphasis on the intersection of business and spirituality. Join us to connect with like-minded individuals and share your business

name: Let's cook together! social cooking experience
description: Wanna learn authentic recipes straight from the source? Looking for a fun interactive event? Got a date you wanna impress? New in town and need to meet people?Join us as one of our native home cooks or experts reveals secrets that produce that authentic flavor! Not only will you learn how it's done, but you will be a part of the process! Tasty meal, new skills, fun company and great memories guaranteed!

name: KhushATX - South Asian / Desi LGBTQ
description: Welcome to KhushATX! We are so glad you found us!! :) We are an active (since 2012) South Asian gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, and queer (LGBTQ) group in the Austin area catering to individuals of Indian, Pakistani, Nepali, Sri Lankan, Bangladeshi, and other South Asian descents. This is a social group where we meet and participate in social events, enjoy each other's company and build friendships. Some of the types of events we have are potlucks, chai-gupshups, and dance events.The group is helped by part-time volunteers, helpers and members. If you'd like to reach a volunteer, please reach out to

name: VegAustin Meetups
description: Welcome to VegAustin! We welcome vegans, vegetarians, and omnivores who want to learn about the benefits of a plant-based diet. We enjoy dining at veg-friendly restaurants, going to special events, and attending happy hours and cooking classes together. Bring a friend or relative. Everyone's welcome!We especially encourage people who are "veg-curious" to come to one of our Meetups and find out how good vegan food can be.

name: Austin Weekday Morning Italian Language Meetup Group
description: The purpose of this group is to create a happy, cheery, daytime coffee meetup to practice our Italian language skills. It's open to any levels of Italian including former students, current students, native speakers and anyone who speaks some Italian. We meet most, but not all, Wednesday mornings and starting November 2, we will meet at Central Market South. While many of us are learning and practicing Italian, we truly appreciate any native speakers as well so that we can hear your beautiful language.

name: A Gente Fala
description: Você já fala Português? Wanting to learn? Either way this group is a place for you to practice in a casual setting, have fun speaking and learning Portuguese! We will meet every other Tuesday at a bar/cafe. Nos vemos lá! :) vai ser bom demais!Esse grupo é um espaço para praticar/conversar num ambiente casual e diverte-se falando e aprendendo português. Vamos encontrar cada 15 dias nas terças num bar ou cafe. Até logo <3

name: Austin LangChain - AI & LLM
description:
Welcome to the Austin LangChain Enthusiasts Meetup Group!
Are you a AI / LLM enthusiast who finds the power of LangChain fascinating? Are you currently learning and utilizing this innovative technology? Look no further! Our meetup group is the perfect platform for you to connect with like-minded individuals in the Austin area who share your passion for LangChain.
Whether you're a beginner eager to dive into the world of LangChain or an experienced user looking to expand your knowledge, our group provides an inclusive and supportive environment for all levels of expertise. Join us to engage in enlightening discussions, share valuable insights, and collaborate on exciting projects related to LangChain.
Here's what you can expect from our meetup group:
Informative Presentations:We regularly host presentations by industry experts, researchers, and practitioners who will share their expertise and insights into the latest advancements in LangChain. These talks will cover various aspects, including best practices, practical applications, and future trends.
Hands-on Workshops:Get ready to roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty! We organize interactive workshops that allow you to put your knowledge into practice. Learn how to leverage LangChain effectively through practical exercises, coding sessions, and collaborative problem-solving activities.
Networking Opportunities:Connect with fellow language enthusiasts, developers, researchers, and professionals who are passionate about LangChain. Expand your professional network, exchange ideas, and foster meaningful connections that can potentially lead to exciting collaborations or career opportunities.
Project Showcases:Share your LangChain projects and see what others have been working on. Our group provides a platform for members to showcase their creations, seek feedback, and receive support and encouragement from the community. This is a fantastic opportunity to gain inspiration, learn from others, and contribute to the growth of the LangChain ecosystem.
Q&A Sessions and Discussions:Have burning questions or specific topics you'd like to explore? Our meetups include interactive Q&A sessions and group discussions where you can seek clarifications, share your experiences, and engage in thought-provoking conversations about LangChain and its applications.
Join us today and become part of the vibrant Austin LangChain community! Let's learn, collaborate, and shape the future of language technology together. Whether you're a student, professional, researcher, or simply a curious individual, we welcome everyone with open arms. Together, we'll unlock the true potential of LangChain and revolutionize the way we interact with languages.
Note:This meetup group is conducted in English, and proficiency in LangChain is not a prerequisite for participation. We believe in creating an inclusive environment where everyone can learn and grow together.
